# Installation {#sec-install}

## Package

Install `sconjoint` from GitHub. Because it contains C++ code, installing it requires a compiler:
Xcode command-line tools on macOS, Rtools on Windows, or a standard build toolchain on Linux.

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("xuyiqing/sconjoint")
```

The package requires R 4.1 or later along with four dependencies: `Rcpp`, `withr`, `digest`, and
`spacefillr`, which supplies scrambled Sobol points for numerical integration. The book's figures
use base R graphics.

```{r}
#| label: load
#| cache: false
library(sconjoint)
packageVersion("sconjoint")
```

```{r}
#| label: render-revision
#| cache: false
#| echo: false
rev <- tryCatch(system2("git", c("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE),
                error = function(e) character(0), warning = function(e) character(0))
rev <- if (length(rev)) rev[1] else "unknown"
```

This book was rendered with sconjoint `r packageVersion("sconjoint")`, from source revision
`r rev` of the package repository.

Three datasets ship with the package:

- `gs2020`: the democracy experiment of @graham2020democracy (@sec-gs).
- `br2017`: the tax-plan experiment of @ballard2017structure (@sec-br).
- `simconjoint`: a simulated candidate-choice experiment with known tastes, 800 respondents who each
  choose between two candidates ten times. Its companion `simconjoint_truth` holds the parameters
  that generated the choices, each respondent's true tastes, and the population values the
  estimates should recover. It needs no saved fits: @sec-quickstart fits the model to it live and
  compares every estimate with the truth.

`sc_example_data()` converts `gs2020` and `br2017` into the paper's model inputs.

```{r}
#| label: data-list
data(package = "sconjoint")$results[, c("Item", "Title")]
```

## Saved fits

Fitting the model at the paper's settings takes hours, with most of that time spent on each
held-out respondent's information (@sec-inference) rather than on training the network. The paper's
fold states are therefore saved, in two files:

| File | Application | Taste factors | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gs_q3.rds` | Graham and Svolik (2020) | 3 | 42,951,896 bytes |
| `br_q4.rds` | Ballard-Rosa, Martin and Scheve (2017) | 4 | 20,506,732 bytes |

The checksums for these files are:

- `gs_q3.rds`: MD5 `17d0f2efa2ecf7c4b2ce3b01991a893b`; SHA-256
  `82ec4e8005d2979f8352d65d3104ea6d503542be005ed1c352658819af845731`.
- `br_q4.rds`: MD5 `6293fd6938d20477369b4f583c986a43`; SHA-256
  `0aa879eadc4ed744ec508dd26fc7a85521326c3f8f8d107c03dd56e8fd245faa`.

For each of the five folds, a file stores what `sc_estimate()` needs along with that fold's network
and covariate scaling. It also holds the respondent ids, groups, folds, and validation respondents
(used to stop training early), together with a checksum of its contents that `sc_load()` verifies.

Because the files are too large for the package, they are published with the GitHub release
[`fits-2026-11`](https://github.com/xuyiqing/sconjoint/releases/tag/fits-2026-11). The code below
downloads both files into a folder `fits` and checks them:

```{r}
#| label: fits-download
#| eval: false
base <- "https://github.com/xuyiqing/sconjoint/releases/download/fits-2026-11"
files <- c("gs_q3.rds", "br_q4.rds")
md5 <- c("17d0f2efa2ecf7c4b2ce3b01991a893b", "6293fd6938d20477369b4f583c986a43")
dir.create("fits", showWarnings = FALSE)
options(timeout = max(600, getOption("timeout")))
for (f in files) download.file(file.path(base, f), file.path("fits", f), mode = "wb")
unname(tools::md5sum(file.path("fits", files))) == md5   # both TRUE
```

**Provenance.** These files hold the paper's selected-rank fits, trained on 14 November 2026 at
package revision `1f7567a` (in the repository's history) on the paper's inputs, which
`sc_example_data()` rebuilds exactly from the bundled data; the folds and validation respondents
are stored in the files as well. On 25 November 2026, each application's fold states and fit files
were packed into one file with `sc_save()` under package version 0.4.0.9000. Checks on the packed
files confirmed that `sc_load()` returns fold states identical to the originals and that each
fold's stored network reproduces its stored mean tastes exactly.

Each file keeps these records (`package_version` and `fit_sha` inside it). Because they describe
the archived fits, the records stay as they are, and later package versions read the files
unchanged.

@sec-gs, @sec-br, @sec-inference and @sec-respondents read the saved files from the folder
specified in the `sconjoint.fits` option, which defaults to `fits` in the working directory. To use
another folder, set the option first:

```{r}
#| label: fits-option
#| eval: false
options(sconjoint.fits = "~/Downloads/sconjoint-fits")
```

Because each chapter runs in its own R session, put that line in an `.Rprofile` file in the book's
folder to render the book with the fits elsewhere.

```{r}
#| label: fits-check
fits <- getOption("sconjoint.fits", "fits")
file.exists(file.path(fits, c("gs_q3.rds", "br_q4.rds")))
gs <- sc_load(file.path(fits, "gs_q3.rds"))
gs
```

The printout reports the rank $q$, the number of folds, respondents and coded features, and the
integration settings used for the information and the scores. If the file is missing, `sc_load()`
returns `NULL` with a message; if the checksum does not match, it stops.
